findings.finding: The machine field owned_by still names the superseded node name 'F2' for both SCC classes (lines 267 and 338; also hypothesis text lines 264 and 335, scope_statement line 45, and line 340 'fixed by F2/L1'), while provenance.schema_owner for the same classes names the canonical nodes F2a/F2b (lines 314 and 383) and the artifact's own rev5 note (line 17) calls F2 'the superseded node name'. A reader or tool resolving owned_by cannot tell whether it means the retired merged node schemas/af_scc_regularities.yaml or the F2a/F2b pair; the two SCC classes would resolve to different owners if the tokens were made explicit.

findings.finding: The scalar class declares genericity_kind: "unresolved" and genericity_value_status "unresolved_pending_L1" (lines 393, 395), but its conclusion quantifies over 'a comeager set G of data' (line 414), which is Baire-residual vocabulary and matches the provisional_baire_residual token used by the other three classes (lines 169, 253, 324). Two readers would disagree on whether the scalar class has already committed to Baire genericity or has none: the field_vocabulary rule at line 144 says a generic-quantified claim must name genericity_kind and genericity_topology, and 'unresolved' names neither the topology nor a provisional value.
findings.remedy: Either set genericity_kind: "provisional_baire_residual" for this class, or replace 'comeager' in the scalar conclusion with an explicit placeholder (e.g. 'a genericity set G whose notion is unresolved and owned by L1') so the conclusion and the axes agree.

findings.finding: G7 reads 'conclusion_type == theorem requires artifact_refs with sha256 and a reviewer verdict', but in this artifact conclusion_type is a three-valued class vocabulary (weak_cosmic_censorship, strong_cosmic_censorship_C2, strong_cosmic_censorship_C0; lines 148-153) that never takes the value 'theorem'. As written the guard cannot fire on any document governed by this vocabulary, so a linter implementing it literally is vacuous; two readers would disagree on whether G7 governs class-level conclusion_type or the claim-level conclusion_type defined in comms/PROTOCOL.md.
findings.remedy: Rewrite G7 to name the field scope explicitly, e.g. 'a claim whose claim-level conclusion_type == theorem requires artifact_refs with sha256 and a reviewer verdict (comms/PROTOCOL.md rule 2)'.

findings.finding: The SET variant asserts 'Strictly stronger than the parent class' (line 94) and justifies only the easy implication (gamma outside the union implies no single q sees a tail). The forward implication actually used (single-q tail implies union containment) requires the causality/transitivity step along gamma, and the strictness is asserted without a witness; the registered falsifier (lines 101-104) is precisely 'show the two readings equivalent', i.e. strictness is an open claim. A reader can invert the direction from the present text.
findings.remedy: State the implication explicitly ('a single-q tail lies in the union by transitivity of the causal relation along gamma; the converse can fail because the union may cover different parts of gamma with different q') and mark strictness as unproven pending the registered falsifier.

findings.finding: The CH variant says 'Strictly weaker than the parent class (a subset of extensions suffices to refute it)' (line 110). The parenthetical's pronoun 'it' reads as CH, while the subset-of-extensions argument is about refuting the parent (any extension refutes the parent; only a Cauchy-horizon-crossing extension refutes CH). Two readers can derive opposite directions from the sentence.
findings.remedy: State the implication direction without a pronoun: 'parent ⟹ CH; the converse fails because only Cauchy-horizon-crossing extensions refute CH'.
